modification_description: Clarify that 'veto power' applies to pace, timing, and scope of change—not an indefinite right to block any worship evolution permanently. Traditional members gain genuine approval power over how and when changes are introduced (e.g., phased trials, limited adoption periods), but this does not constitute an absolute ban on any evolution. The pastor retains leadership responsibility to propose options and move forward when sufficient trust and shared discernment are achieved.
